messages:
deploybot: deploybot paused Release v2.14.0 -> prod: env parity check failed: SERVICE_AUTH_HMAC encoding mismatch between staging and prod. see logs: https://deploybot/reports/4071234567 :eyes:

alex: what exactly is mismatched? staging vs prod encoding details please

maria: quick summary — staging secret was stored as standard base64 without padding, prod was stored as base64url (hyphen/underscore) with padding. our new libauth v1.8 expects standard base64 (with '=' padding). reproducer on canary: `curl -sS https://canary/api/health | jq .auth` shows verifier errors.

kevin: can confirm — canary returned 401s hitting model cache: signature verification fails. snippet from ingress logs:
```
AuthError: invalid signature: unexpected character at position 3
  at verifySignature (/app/lib/auth.js:212:15)
  at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:94:5)
```

bri_sre: we've seen a variation of this in a previous rollout. there used to be a normalization shim that accepted both base64 and base64url; it was removed to tighten validation.

alex: so our options are: rollback runtime image, reintroduce shim (hotpatch), or normalize secrets to the expected format. thoughts?

maria: normalization is fastest for prod-critical apps but requires secret write access + brief downtime for secret rotation metadata. hotpatch (runtime env toggle) is lower-change but needs code toggle and a short-lived fallback. rollback is safest but slower for customers.

jen: product ok with hotpatch + normalization as long as we document and include a rollback trigger in the release notes. we do NOT want to rollback unless errors spike.

kevin: propose sequence:
1) apply runtime fallback env to canary only: `AUTH_ACCEPT_BASE64URL=true` (kubectl patch deployment canary-ingress -n canary --patch '...')
2) backfill/normalize prod secret to standard base64 using safe re-encode command below
3) monitor canary for 30m; if auth errors <0.5% proceed to prod rollout
4) remove fallback after 24h once we confirm no regressions

maria: backfill snippet (preview in staging first):
```
# decode current secret and re-encode to standard base64 (pad with =)
kubectl -n prod get secret service-auth -o jsonpath='{.data.SERVICE_AUTH_HMAC}' | base64 --decode | base64
# then update the secret value (use sops/CI pipeline to record change)
kubectl -n prod patch secret service-auth --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/SERVICE_AUTH_HMAC","value":"<new-base64-value>"}]'
```

alex: decision: Do canary hotpatch + normalize prod secret. rollback if auth errors >0.5% for 15m or if model cache error rate >1%. I'll own coordination and release note text.

maria: on it, applying canary env override now :thumbsup:

bri_sre: I'll add a short runbook and rollback command to the release thread.

kevin: once canary looks good I'll roll the env override and secret change to prod via gradual promotion.

jen: add note to release notes: "Auth secret encoding normalization applied; runtime accepts legacy base64url for 24h while secrets are normalized. If your integration sends base64url, please rotate to standard base64."

deploybot: deploybot resumed canary for v2.14.0 with env override AUTH_ACCEPT_BASE64URL=true. image: redwood/runtime:v2.14.0-hotfix-enc-20260321. Monitoring enabled.

alex: thanks team, stand by for metrics.
